docker-compose-k8s-converter.assumptionNote: Only image, ports, environment, and restart are converted; everything else in the compose file is ignored.
benefits: Moves a compose-based app toward Kubernetes without hand-writing manifests.
Each service becomes a Deployment plus a ClusterIP Service with matching labels.
Port mappings translate to containerPort and Service port/targetPort pairs.
Environment variables become proper env entries in the container spec.
Restart policies map to the closest Kubernetes restartPolicy.

faqs.a: Paste your docker-compose.yml into the input box. The tool parses the services block and generates one Deployment and one Service per service. Download the YAML and apply it with kubectl apply -f k8s-manifests.yaml.
faqs.q: How do I deploy the generated manifests?

faqs.a: unless-stopped and always become restartPolicy: Always, on-failure becomes OnFailure, and no becomes Never. Note that Deployments always use Always in practice; adjust the policy if you generate a Pod or Job.
The Service port is the host side of the mapping and targetPort is the container side. For 8080:80, the Service listens on 8080 and forwards to container port 80.
List entries like - NODE_ENV=production become env name/value pairs. Map-style environment blocks are supported too. Secrets are not created — move sensitive values to Kubernetes Secrets manually.
No. Volumes are intentionally skipped because host paths rarely exist on cluster nodes. Create PersistentVolumeClaims for your data and attach them to the generated Deployments.
Yes, as long as it uses the common subset: services with image, ports, environment, and restart. Exotic keys are ignored rather than breaking the parse.
faqs.q: Will it handle my real compose file?

docker-compose-k8s-converter.formula:
compose service  ->  Deployment + Service
  image: X        ->  containers[0].image: X
  ports "H:C"     ->  containerPort: C, Service port: H, targetPort: C
  environment     ->  env: [{name, value}]
  restart         ->  restartPolicy (Always / OnFailure / Never)
howTo: Paste your docker-compose.yml into the input box.
Check the parsed summary: service count and generated resources.
Review the generated Deployment and Service manifests.
Copy the output or download k8s-manifests.yaml.
Apply with kubectl apply -f k8s-manifests.yaml and adjust as needed.
keyFacts: A Kubernetes Deployment manages a set of identical Pods running your container image.
A Service gives those Pods a stable network identity inside the cluster.
containerPort documents which port the container listens on; the Service port is what others call.
Environment entries map one-to-one to env name/value pairs in the container spec.
The parser handles the common compose subset: image, ports, environment, restart.
docker-compose-k8s-converter.keywords: docker compose to kubernetes, compose to k8s converter, kompose online, docker to kubernetes yaml

labels.errorInvalid: Could not parse a valid compose file. Check the YAML and try again.

limitations: Volumes are not converted — host paths do not exist on cluster nodes.
build:, depends_on:, networks:, and healthchecks are ignored.
Secrets are never generated; move sensitive env values to Kubernetes Secrets.
The YAML parser covers the common subset, not the full compose specification.

docker-compose-k8s-converter.quickAnswer: Teams outgrow docker compose when they move to Kubernetes, but rewriting every service as manifests by hand is tedious. This tool parses your compose file and generates a Deployment and a ClusterIP Service for each service, translating images, port mappings, environment variables, and restart policies.
docker-compose-k8s-converter.tagline: Turn docker-compose.yml into Kubernetes Deployments and Services.
docker-compose-k8s-converter.workedExample:
Input:
services:
  web:
    image: nginx:1.25
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    environment:
      - NODE_ENV=production
    restart: unless-stopped

Output (k8s-manifests.yaml):
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Always
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: nginx:1.25
          ports:
            - containerPort: 80
          env:
            - name: NODE_ENV
              value: "production"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  selector:
    app: web
  type: ClusterIP
  ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
      targetPort: 80

Apply with kubectl apply -f k8s-manifests.yaml.
